scenario: [LIMP.3.3.4]: a `math` member is reached qualified, `math.sqrt` after `import math`, or bare, `sqrt` after `from math import sqrt`, and the two are one builtin. The file imports `math` both ways. Rule `agree` fires where `math.sqrt(t.v) == sqrt(t.v)` and `sqrt(t.v) == 3.0`; rule `pi_is_math` fires where `t.v > math.pi`, `math.pi` the constant the module's source declares. One T with v 9.0: both fire, in source order. A compiler that resolved only one spelling refuses the other as an unknown function or name; one that gave them two different operations would not answer `==`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.resolve`'s rewrite of `math.sqrt(...)` (step 2 of [LGRA.22.9]) and of the bare-imported `sqrt(...)` to the one [LEXP.17.2] row `math.sqrt`, lowered by `dsc.rete`'s `scalar_fn` to FN_SQRT in both places; `math.pi` through `lgra_22_9_library_member` and `stdlib/math.ds`.
rules_ds:
import math
from math import sqrt

schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    v: Float mutable

rule agree:
    T t where math.sqrt(t.v) == sqrt(t.v) and sqrt(t.v) == 3.0
->
    log info "agree"

rule pi_is_math:
    T t where t.v > math.pi
->
    log info "above pi"
